reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that cognition operates within bounded rationality—agents cannot access an objective 'outside reality' independent of their behavioral imperatives. This leads to three key primitives: (1) the fundamental unknowability of reality beyond our needs, (2) the neural substrate for storing learned habits, and (3) the genetic-modulatory relationship between instincts and reflexes. These map naturally to GSI's conformal inference (where models must account for unknown distributions) and GSE's situational reasoning (where agents selectively process information based on utility). The failure mode occurs when behavioral needs are absent, collapsing the system into pure observation.
